sections.overview: Ingerophrynus gollum is a species of bufonid toad known from Peninsular Malaysia.
sections.identification: The original description reported three adult males, 27–30 mm in snout–vent length, with a large head and slender body and limbs.
sections.habitat: It has been recorded in lowland forest at Endau-Rompin and later at Sungai Tua.
sections.diet: The species accounts reviewed do not document its prey.
sections.behavior: The type-series males called in the early evening after brief afternoon rain, from dead vegetation close to the streambed.
sections.reproduction: Males produce a low, two-part raspy call; the reviewed sources do not describe its eggs or larval development.
sections.ecology: Its close congener I. divergens is central to an unresolved taxonomic question: a 2019 molecular study found very low sequence divergence and suggested they may be conspecific.
sections.conservation: A 2018 Malaysian amphibian assessment reported it as globally Endangered and recommended in-situ research; this status predates the later locality records.
